cryo.explain: CP4 quoted 934 kW = the INSTALLED input (operating x 1.25) and 776 kW for LOW, which mixed the scaled production rejection with installed nuclear terms: two bases, not a lost energy flow. Now every watt has one destination: 900 kW of operating input from the L2 bus plus 7021 W lifted from the cold stages leave as 907 kW into LOW at 320 K (the input is 7 % above the 300 K value because the coolers reject warmer). At full installed capacity (re-cool after a fault) LOW sees 1133 kW for hours, inside its 20 % margin.

electrical.note: The H6a pumps (10 MW) run from L1 in a burn. With the pickup lost they must come from L2 (8.7 MW EOL, demand ~5.5 MW): they cannot all run, so a pickup fault means a controlled drive shutdown (decay heat goes to the H6a at part flow, 0.15 of the pump power, which L2 can carry). This is an existing Phase V/VI rule and is stated here, not solved.

l2_failure.case: one NaK loop of unit 1 lost (unit feeds only its own blade): fixed split loads that blade to 125 %

sequence: 0 s: loop low-flow trip on the faulted unit
< 2 s: flow-control valves rebias the neighbouring units (67/33 class)
< 5 s: TAC bypass sets the faulted unit back (turbine bypass to the recuperator); the overloaded blade gains < 50 K in 92 s
1-3 min: reactor ramp-down of the faulted unit to hot standby (decay heat on its own loop A)
L2 load shedding of discretionary loads if the demand band is above the derated output

recovery: isolate the failed loop (isolation valves at the root and the gas cooler)
diagnose: EM pump ORU swap (robot, coast) or a leak (drain to the NaK reserve, sectional repair = yard if the leak is in the casing-hull annulus)
refill, warm the loop with the unit's decay heat, rebias, return to strategy C

pickup_fault.doctrine: DR-C-03 APPROVED (Track F1 operational doctrine): an L1 pickup failure in a burn ends the burn by a controlled propulsion shutdown; continued full-power propulsion is not required
sequence: 0 ms: pickup fault detected (bus undervoltage + converter trip); L1 bus isolators open; the essential drive-services bus transfers to the L2 tie and the defense buffer (automatic transfer < 50 ms)
0-2 s: drive shutdown command; fuel feed throttled to zero; magnet and pulse systems to safe discharge (own stores)
0-30 s: H6a pumps ramp from full flow (10.1 MW) to the decay part flow (1.51 MW); the buffer bridges the gap above the L2 surplus (82 MJ of 209 MJ)
> 30 s: L2 carries the part-flow pumps and all essential loads; heat pumps off; reactive defense limited to buffer bursts after recharge
cooldown: the drive and the HOT loop reject the drive decay and stored heat at part flow; restart only after the pickup is restored
requirements: L2-to-drive-services bus tie rated >= 3.0 MW continuous, automatic transfer < 50 ms
defense buffer reserves >= 82 MJ (with 2x margin 165 MJ) for the shutdown bridge whenever the drive runs
H6a pump drives accept a 30 s ramp to 15 % flow from a 3.0 MW (EOL) L2 surplus
essential loads on the services bus: control, protection, coolant circulation and survival (list below)
essential: H6a pumps at decay part flow (15 %)
L2 NaK pumps and TAC auxiliaries
protection: forward defense sensors, shield cooling, buffer standby
ECLSS, cabins, cryocoolers at operating input
pickup_fault.open: the real shutdown transient (drive heat decay, HOT loop at part flow, Li freeze margins) and the cooldown are NOT verified: problem C-01 stays OPEN (owner: ISSA thermal with Track R)
